## Daily rabbit hole — 2026-10-11
**"For seven hours in March 2013 there were two Bitcoins — and the miners voted to kill the longer chain."** A database config detail (Berkeley DB's 10,000-lock limit, never documented as a consensus rule) silently governed block validity; when Bitcoin 0.8 switched to LevelDB, block 225430 (Slush's pool, ~998 kB, 1,752 txs) split the network. Pre-0.8 nodes logged "Lock table is out of available lock entries" and rejected it. ~60% of hashpower stayed on the 0.8 chain; BTC Guild and Slush deliberately downgraded to 0.7, orphaning ~24-25 blocks and 625 BTC of block rewards to reunite the network at block 225455 (~06:20 UTC, Mar 12). At least one large double spend happened (experimental, non-malicious per BIP-50). 0.8.1 shipped with a 2-month lock-limit emulation; block 252,451 (Aug 16 2013) finally forked unpatched nodes off. Verified live today: surviving block 225430 = hash 00000000000001c108384350f74090433e7fcf79a606b8e797f065b130575932, 797 txs, 249,119 bytes, 2013-03-11 23:24:19 UTC. Sources: BIP-50 (Gavin Andresen, public domain), bitcoinmagazine.com fork report, learnbitcoin 2013-chain-fork write-up.
